call_points.text: Raw material prices stayed elevated versus FY26, with only a marginal sequential rise over Q4FY26.
Utility costs rose significantly versus FY26 on higher fuel prices from the West Asia geopolitical crisis.
Exports were about 60% of Q1FY27 revenue; export and domestic demand both improved.
Q1FY26 had a ₹6.98 Cr business interruption settlement booked as an exceptional item; Q1FY27 had none.
Demand remains stable with cooperative customers accepting short-term pricing amid freight and raw material volatility.
All manufacturing facilities run at full utilization; JNPA SEZ commercial production expected in second half of 2028.
Top-line growth expected to remain very flat until the JNPA SEZ and US plants are commissioned.

timeline.summary: Fine Organic Industries received an income-tax demand order of ₹0.56 Cr for AY 2016-17 and filed an appeal.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹625.32 Cr (+3.1% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹117.49 Cr (+21.0% YoY).

Fine Organic Industries reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹625.32 Cr (+3.1% YoY) and PAT of ₹117.5 Cr (+21.0% YoY), and approved the proposed acquisition of an 80% stake in Malaysia's Oleofine Organics for ₹83 Cr.
Fine Organic Industries Limited shared the earnings call recording for Q4FY26 on May 21, 2026, at 3:30 PM IST via its website.
Fine Organics reported FY26 revenue of ₹2,365 Cr (+4.3% YoY) and PAT of ₹417 Cr (+1.6% YoY), and approved an 80% stake acquisition in Malaysia's Oleofine Organics for ₹82.9 Cr.
Fine Organic's August 2026 investor presentation showed Q1FY27 consolidated revenue up 18% YoY to ₹694 Cr and EBITDA up 42% to ₹176 Cr, with gross margin at 45.4%.
Fine Organic disclosed an inspection and search proceeding initiated by Maharashtra State GST officials under Section 67 of the MGST Act, 2017.
